simple.inThisVerse: The selected word is tied to רְאֵם (H7214) in the Hebrew source text. Part of speech: n-m.
simple.whyItMatters: This word appears 9 times in the Hebrew Bible, so BibleIQ can compare how Scripture uses it across multiple passages.
simple.summary: רְאֵם (rᵉʼêm) means a wild bull (from its conspicuousness) First listed occurrence: Deut 33 17.

definitions.full: H7214. reem רְאֵם noun masculine Job 39:10 wild ox (Assyrian rêmu Dl HWB 603 ( ראם ), Houghton TSBA v (1877). 336 ff., and illustrated before p. 33 Schr KGF 135 ff. , 530 Hom NS 237 ff., 410, 436 f. Dr Deut 33:17 ; on strength and ferocity, Plin NH viii. 21 ; Aramaic רֵימָנָא רֵימָא, רְאֵמָא, (Lag BN 58 ); Arabic is white antelope , antilope leucoryx; ᵐ5 (erroneous) μονοκέρως ( Isa 34:7 ἅδροι , ᵑ9 unicornis , and (oftener) rhinoceros ); — absolute ׳ר Num 23:22 +, רְאֵים Psa 92:11 , רֵים Job 39:9-10 , plural רְאֵמִים Isa 34:7 ; Psa 29:6 , רֵמִים 22:22 (see Baer); — wild ox , as fierce and strong Job 39:9-10 , simile of strength of Israel, ר ׳כְּתוֺעֲפוֺת לוֺ Num 23:22 = 24:8 (JE), קַרְנִי כִּרְאֵם וַתָּרֶם Psa 92:11 ; so figurative of Joseph, ר ׳קַרְנֵי קַרְנַיו Deut 33:17 ; figurative of princes of Edom Isa 34:7 ( + אַבִּירִים עִם מָּרִים ); of powerful foes, רֵמִים מִקַּרְנֵי Psa 22:22 ; in simile of skipping, leaping, בֶּןרְֿאֵמִים 29:6 (|| עֵגֶּל ).
definitions.rootNote: or רְאֵים lemma רְאיֵם second vowel, corrected to רְאֵים ; or רֵים ; or רֵם ; from 7213 ;
